messages:
andrew: Observed a reproducible stall pattern when serving longctx (>=32k) Mixtral and Qwen requests. Throughput drops ~35% and some lanes hit >500ms extra tail latency. Perf traces attached below.
sara: Repro steps? CI test or customer traffic?
andrew: Seen in internal perf harness and a customer trace (redacted). Minimal repro: steady stream of mixed short vs long requests, kernel selector starts switching kernels every few steps, and KV eviction churn spikes.
jin: This sounds like kernel selector oscillation + KV thrash. We saw similar when batcher fed variable seq lengths with bimodal dist.
perf-bot: perf snapshot: model=mixtral-8b, bs=4 steady, ctx=32768, avg p50=82ms, p99=420ms, tokens/s down 37%. profile highlight: repeated kernel recompile/hotswap events.
andrew: Key findings from pprof: heavy time in kernel_selector::choose_kernel() and kv_cache::evict_if_needed() loops. The selector chooses a low-latency kernel for short prefix then flips to a high-throughput kernel mid-query when estimated remaining tokens jumps, causing internal state rebinds.
sara: Do we have a threshold hysteresis? Sounds like we need sticky kernel choice per-request or per-sequence-group.
jin: Current heuristic: choose by estimated seq_len and batch_avg. No per-request stickiness. We can add a per-request sticky flag and cooldown window (N steps or T ms).
andrew: Also noticed RoPE scale interactions for qwen: when we scale RoPE to 1.05 for longctx the attention kernel falls back to a slower path on CUDA due to incompatible kernel path (we hit a non-optimized rotary branch). That amplifies latency when kernel switch happens.
ops: Any quick mitigations we can roll? Canary config?
sara: Short-term: 1) enable per-request kernel stickiness for 10 steps 2) increase KV cache soft limit by 12% to reduce evictions 3) pin qwen rotary scaling to the optimized codepath when possible (fallback to 1.0 for canary).
jin: I ran a micro-benchmark patch locally: sticky kernel + bumped kv_soft_limit => p50 unchanged, p99 improved 28%, tokens/s recovered ~22%. Sample run: 
```
model: mixtral-8b
config: sticky_kernel_steps=10, kv_soft_limit_pct=112
bs=4, ctx=32768
before: tokens/s=1240, p99=420ms
after: tokens/s=1510, p99=303ms
```
andrew: Nice. We should also add a selector cost model tweak: prefer stable kernel if predicted kernel_swap_cost > expected throughput_gain. Need a quick estimator of kernel_swap_cost (measured from compile/hotswap traces).
perf-bot: Suggestion: maintain per-model swap_cost_histogram, update online. Use EWMA with alpha=0.2.
sara: For model-specific defaults: Llama family ok with shorter stickiness (3 steps) since kernels are cheaper to swap; Mistral/Mixtral require longer stickiness (10-15). Qwen needs rotary-path guard and kv_soft_limit + small head-aware batching.
jin: Head-aware batching? Explain.
sara: If model has heads*kv_dim above threshold we prefer smaller max_batch to avoid kernel path that spills to slow matmul. Practically: if (num_heads * head_dim) > 65536 then cap batch to 8 on A100-80gb. We saw throughput cliff beyond that.
andrew: Also add an admission control rule: if request ctx > 24k and batch contains >1 longctx then route to longctx pool (different kernel config + larger KV allocation). Helps avoid mixed batches causing selector flip.
ops: I'll prepare a canary: route 2% traffic to longctx-pool with sticky_kernel=12, kv_soft_limit=115, head_batch_cap enabled.
deploy-bot: canary created: cluster=canary-longctx-2pct, rollout=0% -> 2% over 30m.
jin: Tests to run before wider rollout: synthetic bimodal seq distribution, steady long-only, 50/50 mixture; validate p50/p95/p99 and cost delta. Also check memory use under kv_soft_limit bump.
andrew: Action items: andrew->produce kernel_swap_cost estimator PR, jin->bench harness for head-aware batch cap, sara->config defaults per-model and canary config, ops->monitoring dashboard for swap_count, kv_evictions, rotary_fallback_count.
sara: I'll include a short blurb for docs: recommended defaults per model family, why stickiness matters, and how head*dim limit interacts with batch size.
andrew: TL;DR: sticky kernel + modest KV soft-limit increase + head-aware batch caps + longctx pool routing gives immediate recovery; longer-term add cost-model to selector and rotary optimized path for qwen.
perf-bot: noted metrics to surface: swap_rate/s, avg_swap_cost_ms, kv_evictions/s, p99_longctx_latency.
ops: I'll watch the canary and post results in this thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:
